symptom: `mxcli check --references` printed `✗ 1 reference error(s) found` and then `0 issues: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info` — the reporter asked why a reference error does not count as an error (mendixlabs/mxcli#1726)
cause: the closing summary sums the `printed` list, which only the `report` helper appends to; the reference tier prints its errors and warnings itself, so they never reached the total
file: cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go (reference tier appends to printed); test cmd/mxcli/check_reference_summary_test.go
insight: When one summary is computed over a list that several tiers feed, a tier with its own print path drops out of the total silently. Only the run in the report had an earlier tier's violation, so the summary line printed at all; a script with nothing but a reference error printed no summary, which is why the test asserts `1 errors` rather than the absence of `0 errors`. Control: without the append, the test fails with no summary in the output.
